geographicScope.boundaryCaveat: The adopted source display outline and UCDB country attribution differ in Crimea. Ukraine-assigned city records are excluded and not reattributed. This subset is not a national population total.

method: Exact ID_UC_G0 join of general CSV, general GeoPackage UC_centroids and GHSL CSV. All source-defined centres assigned by GC_CNT_GAD_2025 to Russia (253 records) are retained. No top-N selection. Source centroid metre coordinates are converted by inverse spherical Mollweide with radius 6378137 m, central meridian and false offsets 0, as declared in the GeoPackage; original negative western longitudes are retained. No nearest-land imputation, raster-derived values, country totals or population rounding.
limitations: Urban centres are publisher-defined population concentrations, not municipalities, all settlements or all capitals.
Population years 2000, 2010 and 2020 use the fixed 2025 urban footprint. Changes do not measure expansion of the urban boundary.
No source-defined centre for a country/territory does not mean zero population. This subset cannot replace a population-distribution grid or national/island population statistics.

Country attribution is exactly source GC_CNT_GAD_2025=Russia. Crimea records remain Ukraine-assigned and are not moved into this subset. Display boundaries may use a different geographic convention. This is not a national population total.

Map consumers must unwrap EPSG:4326 longitudes consistently with the 18 to 191 degree Russia display. The current 253 centres have longitudes 20.5 to 158.6 degrees; absence of a source centre in the far northeast does not mean zero population.
